# Before You Begin: The Questions That Matter {.unnumbered}

Before writing strategy documents or standing up infrastructure, your organization needs an honest, cross-functional conversation about what GeoAI means for you. This chapter raises the questions. The rest of both playbooks help you find the answers.

::: {.callout-note}
## Shared Pre-Chapter
This brainstorming guide appears in both the Decision Maker and Developer playbooks. The best GeoAI programs start with leadership and practitioners thinking through the same issues — from different angles — together. Questions are tagged by the **C-suite role** and **organizational level** they most directly concern, but everyone benefits from reading all of them.
:::

## How to Use This Chapter

Use this as a **workshop guide**. Gather your leadership team and your technical leads in the same room (or the same thread). Work through each section. Don't try to answer everything — flag the questions that are most urgent or most contested, and let those drive the order in which you read the rest of this playbook.

### Role Tags

Questions are tagged to indicate primary ownership. Many questions are relevant across roles, but the tag signals who should **drive the answer**.

| Tag | Role | Focus Area |
|-----|------|------------|
| {{< fa building >}} **CEO** | Chief Executive Officer | Mission alignment, organizational direction, stakeholder communication |
| {{< fa dollar-sign >}} **CFO** | Chief Financial Officer | Budget, ROI, cost modeling, capital allocation, financial risk |
| {{< fa shield >}} **CSO** | Chief Security Officer | Data security, access controls, adversarial threats, clearances, compliance |
| {{< fa microchip >}} **CTO** | Chief Technology Officer | Architecture, platforms, build/buy, engineering standards, technical debt |
| {{< fa globe >}} **CGO** | Chief Geospatial Officer | Geospatial strategy, GIS modernization, spatial data infrastructure, domain alignment |

## 1. Why GeoAI, Why Now, Why Us?

The most dangerous GeoAI programs start with a technology push ("we should be doing AI") rather than a mission pull ("this specific problem would benefit from AI on geospatial data"). Start here.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
**CEO** and **CGO** jointly own this conversation. The CEO ensures GeoAI connects to organizational mission; the CGO ensures the geospatial framing is grounded in reality. The **CFO** must be present to reality-check the cost of both action and inaction.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CEO]** What specific mission outcomes are we failing to achieve — or achieving too slowly — that GeoAI could improve?
- **[CEO]** Is our interest in GeoAI driven by genuine mission need, or by pressure to appear innovative? Can we tell the difference?
- **[CEO]** Can we articulate a GeoAI value proposition in one sentence that a board member, a funder, or a member of the public would understand?
- **[CEO]** How does GeoAI fit into our broader digital transformation and AI strategy — or are we treating it as a standalone initiative?
- **[CFO]** What is the cost of *not* investing in GeoAI? Is there a quantifiable competitive or mission risk to inaction?
- **[CFO]** Do we have a realistic cost model for GeoAI, or are we working from vendor slide decks and conference keynotes?
- **[CGO]** Are our competitors or peer organizations already deploying GeoAI? What specific capabilities are they fielding that we are not?
- **[CGO]** Which of our existing geospatial programs would benefit most from AI augmentation vs. which are working fine as-is?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** Have we done any proof-of-concept work? What did we learn about feasibility, cost, and organizational readiness?
- **[Senior Mgr]** Which existing geospatial workflows are bottlenecks — where analysts spend days doing work that a model could accelerate?
- **[Mid Mgr]** What are the quick wins — problems where GeoAI can deliver measurable value within months, not years?
- **[Mid Mgr]** Is the problem we want to solve actually an AI problem, or is it a data engineering problem, a data access problem, or a staffing problem wearing an AI costume?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** Do we have actual problems where geospatial ML outperforms traditional GIS analysis, or are we looking for a nail for this hammer?
- **[IC]** Which of our daily workflows involve repetitive visual interpretation, manual feature extraction, or pattern recognition that a model could realistically handle?
- **[IC]** Have we benchmarked any AI approaches against our current methods on our own data — not on conference demo data?

---

## 2. Organizational Identity and GeoAI Ambition

How an organization sees itself shapes what it will attempt with GeoAI — and what it should attempt.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
**CEO** sets the ambition level. **CTO** and **CGO** reality-check it against technical and geospatial maturity. **CFO** aligns ambition with budget cycles.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CEO]** Are we a **GeoAI builder** (developing custom models), a **GeoAI buyer** (procuring vendor solutions), or a **GeoAI assembler** (fine-tuning and integrating existing models)? Does our answer match our actual talent and budget, or is it aspirational?
- **[CEO]** Do we have executive sponsorship with staying power, or will this initiative lose funding at the next budget cycle?
- **[CEO]** How much organizational change are we willing to absorb? GeoAI may require new roles, new workflows, and new ways of making decisions.
- **[CFO]** What is our planning horizon — and corresponding budget commitment? A one-time project, a sustained program, or a permanent organizational capability?
- **[CFO]** How do we fund the gap between "proof of concept" and "production capability"? That gap is where most GeoAI programs die.
- **[CTO]** How do we handle the tension between "move fast with AI" and "our organization moves deliberately by design"?
- **[CTO]** Do we have the engineering maturity to support ML in production, or are we still struggling with basic data pipelines and version control?
- **[CGO]** Does our geospatial infrastructure (data, tools, workflows) support AI integration, or does the foundation need work first?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** What is the gap between our proof-of-concept environment and our production environment? Is it a crack or a canyon?
- **[Senior Mgr]** Do we have the institutional patience for the 6-18 months it takes to go from prototype to reliable production model?
- **[Mid Mgr]** Will our organization let teams fail fast and iterate, or does every project need to succeed on the first try?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How much technical debt are we willing to accumulate in the name of speed — and who will pay it down later?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** Are we honest about our starting point? A team that has never deployed a REST API should not plan to deploy real-time geospatial inference next quarter.
- **[IC]** Do we have the skills to execute the ambition being described, or are we going to spend the first year learning fundamentals while leadership expects results?

---

## 3. Data: The Foundation of Everything

Every GeoAI conversation eventually becomes a data conversation. Address this early.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
The **CGO** owns the geospatial data strategy. The **CFO** must understand the cost implications of data acquisition. The **CSO** must weigh in on data security, residency, and classification. The **CTO** owns the infrastructure that stores, catalogs, and serves data.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CGO]** What geospatial data do we already own, license, or have access to? Do we actually have an inventory?
- **[CGO]** What gaps exist between our current data holdings and our GeoAI ambitions — in resolution, coverage, frequency, or labeling?
- **[CGO]** Who is accountable for the quality, accuracy, and currency of our geospatial data holdings?
- **[CFO]** What does our annual geospatial data spend look like, and how would GeoAI change it? Are we modeling the full cost (acquisition + storage + processing + labeling)?
- **[CFO]** What are the licensing implications of using commercial imagery to train AI models? Do our current licenses permit derivative AI products?
- **[CFO]** If we generate AI-derived geospatial products, who owns the intellectual property? Does this vary by data source?
- **[CSO]** Do we have data sovereignty or data residency requirements that constrain where data can be stored and processed?
- **[CSO]** What data classification levels apply to our geospatial holdings? Can classified or sensitive imagery be used for model training, and under what controls?
- **[CTO]** How do we catalog, version, and govern geospatial data at the scale GeoAI requires?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** Are there data sharing agreements with partners that would be affected by AI-derived products?
- **[Senior Mgr]** How do we feel about open data vs. proprietary data? Are we prepared to depend on datasets we don't control?
- **[Mid Mgr]** Do we have labeled training data for our priority use cases, or do we need to create it? Who does the labeling — internal analysts, contractors, or a vendor?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How current does our data need to be for each use case? Is last month's imagery acceptable, or do we need near-real-time?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** Can we actually access our own data programmatically, or is it trapped in desktop GIS projects, disconnected file shares, and someone's external hard drive?
- **[IC]** Is our imagery in cloud-optimized formats (COG, ZARR, cloud-native), or will we spend months on format conversion before any modeling begins?
- **[IC]** How do we handle the sheer volume? A single year of moderate-resolution satellite coverage can be petabytes. Where does it live? How do we search it?
- **[IC]** How do we version datasets that are hundreds of gigabytes or terabytes? What tools are we standardizing on (DVC, LakeFS, catalog versioning)?
- **[IC]** What is our data catalog situation? Can a new team member discover what data exists without asking five people?
- **[IC]** Are our coordinate reference systems consistent, or is every dataset in a different projection?
- **[IC]** Do we have ground truth data for validation, or are we going to validate satellite-derived predictions against other satellite-derived predictions?
- **[IC]** What happens when a data vendor changes their API, pricing, or licensing terms mid-project?

---

## 4. Models: Build, Buy, Fine-Tune, or Prompt?

The AI model landscape is shifting fast. The "right" approach today may not be the right approach in six months.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
The **CTO** and **CGO** co-own model strategy. The CTO drives the technical architecture and build/buy decision. The CGO ensures model choices align with geospatial domain needs. The **CFO** must understand total cost of ownership (training, maintenance, retraining, retirement).
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CTO]** Should we invest in building models from scratch, fine-tuning foundation models, or integrating vendor solutions? What does each path cost in talent, time, and infrastructure?
- **[CTO]** What is our framework and platform strategy — single standard (simplicity) or multi-framework (flexibility)?
- **[CTO]** Are we comfortable with the opacity of some foundation models, or do we require full explainability for our domain?
- **[CGO]** Which geospatial domains (land cover, change detection, object detection, damage assessment) are our highest-priority model targets? Are existing models adequate or do we need custom development?
- **[CFO]** How do we think about model shelf life? AI models degrade as the world changes. Are we budgeting for ongoing retraining and maintenance — not just initial development?
- **[CFO]** What is our vendor strategy for AI models? Single vendor (relationship depth), multi-vendor (risk diversification), or open-source (cost, but self-support)?
- **[CSO]** What is our policy on using open-source models? Are there supply chain security concerns with community-maintained model weights?
- **[CEO]** If a model makes a wrong prediction that leads to a bad decision, who is accountable — the vendor, the developer, the model owner, or the decision maker who acted on the output?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** How do we evaluate commercial GeoAI products? What due diligence is required before procurement — and who has the expertise to conduct it?
- **[Senior Mgr]** What happens if our primary model vendor is acquired, pivots, or raises prices? Do we have a contingency plan?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How do we evaluate model performance in a way that is meaningful to mission stakeholders, not just other data scientists?
- **[Mid Mgr]** What is our experiment tracking standard? Can we reproduce a model from six months ago — data, code, config, and results?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** Which geospatial foundation models are relevant to our use cases (Prithvi, Clay, SatCLIP, IBM/NASA models, etc.)? Have we evaluated any of them on our own data?
- **[IC]** Do we have enough labeled data to fine-tune effectively, or are we in few-shot / zero-shot territory?
- **[IC]** Are we solving a problem that actually needs deep learning, or would a classical ML approach (random forest, gradient boosting) work just as well at a fraction of the cost and complexity?
- **[IC]** How do we handle geospatial-specific modeling challenges — tile boundary effects, scale dependence, spatial autocorrelation that contaminates train/test splits?
- **[IC]** How do we handle multi-modal inputs (optical + SAR + elevation + vector)? Do we have a fusion strategy or are we treating each modality independently?
- **[IC]** Are we planning for spatial cross-validation, or are we going to accidentally overfit by using spatially adjacent tiles in train and test sets?
- **[IC]** What is our strategy for handling clouds, shadows, seasonal variation, atmospheric effects, and other noise in optical imagery?

---

## 5. Governance and Guardrails

Governance done well enables speed. Governance done poorly (or not done at all) eventually causes a crisis.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
The **CEO** sets governance expectations. The **CSO** ensures security and compliance requirements are met. The **CGO** ensures governance is grounded in geospatial domain realities. The **CTO** ensures governance processes are technically feasible and not purely bureaucratic.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CEO]** Do we have an AI governance framework, or are we making it up as we go? Does it cover GeoAI specifically, or only generic AI?
- **[CEO]** What is our Acceptable Use Policy for GeoAI? Are there use cases we will categorically refuse to pursue, regardless of technical feasibility?
- **[CEO]** What is our disclosure policy? Do stakeholders and the public know when a geospatial product was generated by AI rather than a human analyst?
- **[CEO]** How do we handle dual-use concerns — models that could serve beneficial purposes but also enable surveillance, targeting, or other harmful applications?
- **[CSO]** Are we subject to executive orders, regulations, or sector-specific rules about AI use (EU AI Act, US EO 14110, agency-specific AI directives, export controls)?
- **[CSO]** How do we handle Freedom of Information requests, audits, or legal discovery for AI model details, training data, and decision logs?
- **[CSO]** What are the insurance and liability implications of AI-generated geospatial products? Has legal counsel reviewed our exposure?
- **[CTO]** Who has the authority to approve a GeoAI model for production use? Is that authority clear, documented, and understood by every developer?
- **[CGO]** How do we maintain public trust when using AI to generate geospatial products that directly affect communities — zoning, disaster response, environmental monitoring?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** What evidence package is required before a model can be deployed? Is it the same for every model, or tiered by risk?
- **[Senior Mgr]** How often should deployed models be re-reviewed? What triggers an out-of-cycle review?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How do we handle model updates? Does every minor retrain need a full governance review, or is there an expedited path for low-risk changes?
- **[Mid Mgr]** What happens when governance says no? Is there a clear, constructive path to address concerns and resubmit — or does rejection kill the project?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** Do the governance requirements actually make sense technically, or are they checkbox exercises that slow work down without improving safety?
- **[IC]** Can we automate parts of the governance review — automated bias audits, automated model card generation, automated data provenance checks?
- **[IC]** Are governance reviewers technically literate enough to evaluate model artifacts (confusion matrices, ROC curves, bias reports), or do we need to translate everything into slide decks?
- **[IC]** What documentation format does the governance board actually consume? Notebooks? PDFs? Dashboards? Knowing this upfront saves rework.

---

## 6. Responsible AI: Ethics in the Geospatial Context

Geospatial AI raises ethical issues that generic AI ethics frameworks miss. Location data is inherently about people and places — and the stakes are specific.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
The **CEO** owns the organization's ethical posture. The **CGO** translates that posture into geospatial-specific guidelines. The **CSO** addresses privacy and security dimensions. Individual contributors own the technical implementation of fairness testing and bias audits.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CEO]** What is our position on using AI-generated geospatial products for decisions that affect people's lives, livelihoods, or property rights?
- **[CEO]** Do we have the organizational courage to shelve a technically impressive model if the ethical risks outweigh the benefits?
- **[CEO]** Are we considering the communities that appear in our training data and model outputs as stakeholders, or only as data points?
- **[CSO]** High-resolution imagery can reveal personal information — vehicle movements, building occupancy patterns, agricultural practices. Where do we draw the line between useful analysis and surveillance?
- **[CSO]** How do we handle the tension between model transparency ("here's how the model works") and operational security ("we can't reveal our imagery sources or model capabilities")?
- **[CGO]** GeoAI models often perform differently across geographies — better in cities, worse in rural areas; better in the Global North, worse in the Global South. What is our standard for geographic equity?
- **[CGO]** If our model identifies a problem in a community (informal settlements, environmental hazards, infrastructure decay), do we have an obligation to act? To whom?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** How do we staff and fund responsible AI reviews? Is this a dedicated role, a shared responsibility, or an unfunded mandate?
- **[Mid Mgr]** At what stage in the development process do we conduct ethical reviews — before data collection, during development, before deployment, or all three?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** How do we test for geographic bias when we may not have ground truth data in underrepresented regions?
- **[IC]** Are our evaluation metrics capturing fairness across geographies, or just reporting aggregate performance that masks disparities?
- **[IC]** How do we handle temporal bias — models trained on historical data may encode historical inequities (e.g., infrastructure investment patterns, land use classifications)?
- **[IC]** What do we do when a model works well in aggregate but fails badly for specific, identifiable communities?
- **[IC]** How do we communicate uncertainty to users who want definitive answers? Do our outputs include confidence intervals, probability maps, or just hard classifications?
- **[IC]** Are we building in human review checkpoints for high-stakes predictions, or are we letting automation run unchecked?
- **[IC]** What is our approach to model interpretability? Can we explain *why* the model made a specific prediction at a specific location?
- **[IC]** How do we handle adversarial inputs — deliberately crafted imagery or data designed to fool our models?
- **[IC]** Are we tracking the environmental cost of training large geospatial models? GPU compute has a carbon footprint — does our organization care?

---

## 7. Talent, Culture, and Organizational Change

GeoAI is as much a people challenge as a technology challenge. The organizational design decisions in this section will determine whether your GeoAI program thrives or stalls.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
The **CEO** and **CGO** co-own organizational design for GeoAI. The **CFO** owns the compensation and hiring budget. The **CTO** defines technical skill requirements. Every management level owns culture within their span of control.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CEO]** Who owns GeoAI organizationally — the GIS shop, the data science team, IT, a new unit, or a cross-functional team? How do we prevent turf wars?
- **[CEO]** How do we prevent a two-tier culture where "AI people" are seen as elite and traditional analysts feel threatened or devalued?
- **[CFO]** The GeoAI talent market is extremely competitive. Can we compete on compensation, or do we need to compete on mission, flexibility, and culture? What is the total cost of a GeoAI team (salary, compute, data, training, tools)?
- **[CFO]** How do we retain GeoAI talent? What is the cost of attrition — recruiting, onboarding, lost institutional knowledge?
- **[CTO]** What GeoAI roles do we actually need — and how do they differ from generic data science or generic GIS roles?
- **[CTO]** Are our managers and directors technically literate enough to evaluate GeoAI proposals and performance, or are they approving things they don't understand?
- **[CGO]** How do we ensure domain experts — the people who actually understand the geospatial problems — are empowered to shape AI solutions, not just consulted at the end?
- **[CGO]** Do we hire GeoAI specialists, retrain existing geospatial analysts, or both? What is the realistic timeline for upskilling?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** How do we build a hiring pipeline for a role (GeoAI Engineer) that most universities don't explicitly teach?
- **[Senior Mgr]** What is the career path for a GeoAI developer here? If it dead-ends at "senior IC," we will lose people to organizations with better ladders.
- **[Mid Mgr]** Are there enough people to actually do this? Can the team handle new model development while maintaining existing systems and responding to ad-hoc requests?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How do we handle the "single point of failure" problem — when one person becomes the only one who understands a critical model or pipeline?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How do we preserve institutional knowledge? Documentation standards, code reviews, pair programming, knowledge-sharing sessions — what actually works here?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** Do the GIS analysts trust us? Do we trust their domain expertise? Is there a working relationship, or a cultural divide?
- **[IC]** What does professional development look like? Do we get time and budget for learning, conferences, experimentation, and contributing to open source?
- **[IC]** Are we empowered to push back when leadership asks for unrealistic timelines or oversells model capabilities to stakeholders?
- **[IC]** How do we collaborate across time zones, security domains, and organizational boundaries — especially when we can't share data or code freely?

---

## 8. Infrastructure, Compute, and Cloud

GeoAI is computationally expensive and data-intensive. Infrastructure decisions are strategic decisions — and wrong ones are expensive to reverse.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
The **CTO** owns infrastructure architecture and platform decisions. The **CFO** must understand and approve the cost profile — GeoAI compute costs can be orders of magnitude higher than traditional IT. The **CSO** owns security, access control, and data residency enforcement.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CTO]** Cloud, on-premises, or hybrid? What do our security requirements, data residency rules, and operational maturity actually support?
- **[CTO]** What is our cloud vendor strategy — single provider (simpler, lock-in risk) or multi-cloud (flexible, complexity cost)?
- **[CTO]** Are we investing in infrastructure that our team can actually manage, or are we building something that requires a DevOps team we don't have and can't hire?
- **[CFO]** What is the estimated annual compute cost for our GeoAI ambitions? GPU bills may be 10-100x our current compute spend. Have we modeled this?
- **[CFO]** How do we handle burst capacity for model training without paying for idle GPUs the other 90% of the time?
- **[CSO]** How do we handle classified or sensitive data that cannot go to commercial cloud? Is there an on-prem GPU strategy, or a government-cloud option?
- **[CSO]** How do we handle the security implications of GPU-enabled cloud instances that may require broader network access and different security profiles than traditional compute?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** What is our storage strategy? Raw imagery, processed training chips, model checkpoints, and inference outputs all require different storage tiers with different cost profiles.
- **[Senior Mgr]** Can our network bandwidth handle moving terabytes of imagery to our compute environment — or do we need to move compute to the data?
- **[Mid Mgr]** Do we have GPU access today, or do developers submit a request and wait weeks? If access is slow, developers will find workarounds that create shadow IT risks.
- **[Mid Mgr]** Do we have a CI/CD pipeline for ML models, or is "deployment" someone manually copying files to a server?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** What is our actual experience with containerized ML workloads? Can we run a training job on Kubernetes, or are we still running everything on local machines?
- **[IC]** How do we handle reproducibility? Can we rebuild our entire environment — data, code, dependencies, compute configuration — from scratch?
- **[IC]** What is our monitoring story? When a deployed model starts performing poorly, how quickly do we find out — minutes, hours, or when a stakeholder complains?
- **[IC]** Are we optimizing for training cost, inference latency, or both? These often trade off against each other, and the priority should be set by the use case, not by engineering preference.

---

## 9. Partnerships, Procurement, and the Vendor Landscape

No organization builds GeoAI entirely in-house. Partnerships and procurement decisions have long-term consequences that outlast the people who made them.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
The **CEO** owns strategic partnerships. The **CFO** owns procurement and vendor financial risk. The **CSO** evaluates vendor security posture and data handling. The **CTO** evaluates technical integration. The **CGO** evaluates whether vendor claims match geospatial domain reality.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CEO]** What partnerships (academic, industry, government, international) would accelerate our GeoAI program — and what do we bring to the table in return?
- **[CEO]** What is our open-source strategy? Do we contribute back, only consume, or avoid entirely? Each choice has reputational and practical consequences.
- **[CFO]** What procurement vehicles do we have for AI and cloud services? Are they fast enough to keep up with a technology that changes quarterly?
- **[CFO]** How do we handle vendor concentration risk — if our key imagery provider or cloud vendor changes terms, raises prices, or gets acquired?
- **[CSO]** How do we evaluate the security posture of GeoAI vendors — especially startups that may have immature security programs handling our data?
- **[CSO]** Are our partnership and vendor agreements AI-ready? Do they address model ownership, training data rights, derived product rights, and data handling after contract termination?
- **[CTO]** How painful is vendor integration with our existing stack? Is there a realistic estimate of the engineering effort, or are we assuming plug-and-play?
- **[CGO]** How do we evaluate GeoAI vendor claims? The market is full of startups showing impressive demos on cherry-picked examples — who has the domain expertise to separate substance from hype?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** How do we handle intellectual property when co-developing models with partners? Are the agreements clear before development starts?
- **[Senior Mgr]** Are academic partnerships productive, or do they produce papers that don't translate to production? How do we structure partnerships for operational value?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How do we handle the licensing complexity of training on data from multiple sources with different terms? Who tracks this?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** Which vendor APIs have we actually evaluated hands-on, and which are we just assuming will work based on marketing?
- **[IC]** Are vendor benchmarks trustworthy, or do we need to rerun evaluations on our own data before making commitments?
- **[IC]** How do we handle the "vendor lock-in through data format" problem — proprietary formats that make migration expensive?
- **[IC]** When a vendor library has a breaking change, how long does it take us to recover? Do we have insulation layers?
- **[IC]** What is our experience with open-source geospatial AI tools? Are we contributing improvements back, or just consuming — and does that affect how well the tools serve our needs?

---

## 10. Risk, Failure, and Incident Planning

Things will go wrong. The question is whether you have planned for it.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
**Every role and every level** owns this domain. The CEO owns organizational reputation risk. The CFO owns financial exposure. The CSO owns security incidents. The CTO owns technical failure response. The CGO owns domain-specific failure modes. Managers own process and training. ICs own implementation of monitoring, rollback, and alerting.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CEO]** What is the worst-case scenario for a GeoAI failure in our context? (Wrong flood zone? Missed building damage? Misidentified land use that affects property rights? A model that discriminates against specific communities?)
- **[CEO]** What is our communication plan when a model fails publicly? Who speaks, what do they say, and how fast?
- **[CFO]** Do we have insurance coverage for AI-generated geospatial products? What is our financial exposure per incident?
- **[CFO]** Have we budgeted for incident response, model remediation, and potential re-validation — or are we treating these as "if it happens, we'll figure it out"?
- **[CSO]** Are we stress-testing our models against adversarial scenarios — deliberately crafted inputs designed to exploit weaknesses — or only against typical conditions?
- **[CSO]** How do we handle the liability chain — from data provider to model developer to deployment engineer to decision maker to affected community?
- **[CTO]** What is our model retirement strategy? How do we know when to take a model out of service before it causes harm — and who has the authority to pull the trigger?
- **[CGO]** What are the domain-specific failure modes we should be planning for — seasonal performance degradation, sensor changes, geographic transfer failure, land use change?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** Are our SLAs realistic, or did someone promise five-nines availability for a research prototype?
- **[Senior Mgr]** How do we do post-mortems when models fail? Is there a blameless culture, or do failure investigations become blame exercises that discourage transparency?
- **[Mid Mgr]** Do we have rollback procedures? Can we revert to the previous model version within minutes, not days?
- **[Mid Mgr]** Do we ever simulate model failures in staging — fire drills for GeoAI?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** Do we have a kill switch for deployed models? How fast can we disable a model that is producing harmful outputs — and has anyone actually tested the kill switch?
- **[IC]** What does our monitoring actually catch? Are we detecting data drift and prediction distribution shifts, or just waiting for user complaints?
- **[IC]** What is our logging strategy? When something goes wrong, do we have the data to understand *why* — including the exact input data, model version, and inference path?
- **[IC]** How do we handle cascading failures — when model A feeds model B, and model A degrades? Do we have circuit breakers?

---

## 11. Measuring Success and Communicating Value

If you cannot explain the value of your GeoAI program in terms your stakeholders understand, you cannot sustain it.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
The **CEO** owns the narrative. The **CFO** owns ROI metrics and financial justification. The **CGO** owns domain-impact metrics (missions supported, decisions improved, time saved). Middle management and ICs own the technical metrics that feed into business metrics.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CEO]** How do we communicate GeoAI value in terms that non-technical stakeholders — board members, funders, the public — understand?
- **[CEO]** How do we handle the "valley of disillusionment" when early hype meets production reality and the first quarterly report doesn't show the transformative results people expected?
- **[CEO]** How do we communicate both successes and limitations honestly, without either overselling or underselling?
- **[CFO]** How do we measure return on investment for GeoAI? Is it cost savings, speed, accuracy, new capabilities, risk reduction, or all of the above — and can we assign dollar values?
- **[CFO]** Are we measuring what matters, or what is easy to measure? Counting "models deployed" is easy; measuring "decisions improved" is hard but more meaningful.
- **[CGO]** How do we avoid the "demo trap" — impressive proofs of concept that never deliver operational value? What is the bar for "production ready" vs. "impressive demo"?
- **[CGO]** What is our reporting cadence for GeoAI program status? Does it align with organizational planning and budget cycles?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** Can we quantify the time saved or decisions improved by GeoAI vs. traditional approaches? Do we have baseline measurements?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How do we show value during the long, unglamorous data preparation and model development phase — before there are results to report?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How do we handle the "it's only 85% accurate" conversation with stakeholders who expect 100%? Are we equipping leadership with the right framing?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** What metrics do stakeholders actually care about, and how do we surface them — dashboards, reports, alerts, or embedded in existing tools?
- **[IC]** How do we avoid "accuracy theater" — reporting inflated metrics on cherry-picked test sets that don't reflect real-world performance?
- **[IC]** Are we tracking technical metrics (latency, throughput, drift) that we can map to business outcomes (time saved, cost reduced, coverage expanded)?
- **[IC]** What is our strategy for managing expectations? Stakeholders who saw a ChatGPT demo may expect magic from a satellite image classifier.

---

## 12. The Horizon: What is Coming Next?

GeoAI is evolving rapidly. Planning for uncertainty is not optional.

::: {.callout-important}
## Primary Ownership
The **CEO** owns strategic positioning. The **CTO** and **CGO** own technology horizon scanning. The **CSO** monitors emerging regulatory and threat landscapes.
:::

### Executive Leadership

- **[CEO]** How do we position our organization to be a GeoAI leader — shaping the field — rather than a follower who is always catching up?
- **[CEO]** What geopolitical risks could affect our access to satellite data, cloud compute, or AI talent?
- **[CTO]** Are we building flexible, modular architectures, or locking into approaches that will be outdated in two years?
- **[CTO]** How do we plan for the possibility that foundation models make some of our current custom model investments obsolete?
- **[CSO]** What emerging regulations — domestic and international — could affect our GeoAI program? Are we tracking the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and sector-specific guidance?
- **[CSO]** How do we prepare for evolving adversarial threats as GeoAI becomes more widespread and attackers become more sophisticated?
- **[CGO]** How do we stay informed about GeoAI advancements without chasing every trend? What is our evaluation framework for new capabilities?
- **[CGO]** What emerging geospatial data sources (new satellite constellations, drone networks, IoT sensors) could change our assumptions about data availability and cost?

### Senior & Middle Management

- **[Senior Mgr]** How do we keep our team's skills current when the field moves this fast? What is our learning and development budget and policy?
- **[Mid Mgr]** How do we handle the "rewrite vs. iterate" decision when a fundamentally better approach emerges mid-project?

### Individual Contributors

- **[IC]** Are we architecting for modularity — can we swap out a model, a data source, or an inference engine without rebuilding the whole pipeline?
- **[IC]** Are we experimenting with emerging approaches (multimodal models, foundation model prompting, synthetic data generation, agentic workflows) at low risk?
- **[IC]** What would it take to incorporate real-time or near-real-time geospatial AI into our workflows — and is that even necessary for our use cases?
- **[IC]** Are we documenting our architectural decisions so future developers understand not just *what* was built but *why* it was built that way?

## Using This Guide

### By Role

| If You Are... | Start With These Domains | Then Read These Playbook Chapters |
|---------------|-------------------------|----------------------------------|
| **CEO** | 1 (Why GeoAI), 2 (Identity), 5 (Governance), 7 (Talent), 11 (Measuring Success) | Strategy, Governance, Investment |
| **CFO** | 1 (Why GeoAI), 2 (Identity), 3 (Data), 7 (Talent), 8 (Infrastructure), 11 (Success) | Strategy, Investment, Data Strategy |
| **CSO** | 3 (Data), 5 (Governance), 6 (Responsible AI), 8 (Infrastructure), 9 (Vendors), 12 (Horizon) | Governance, Risk Management |
| **CTO** | 2 (Identity), 3 (Data), 4 (Models), 8 (Infrastructure), 12 (Horizon) | *All Developer Playbook chapters* |
| **CGO** | 1 (Why GeoAI), 3 (Data), 4 (Models), 6 (Responsible AI), 7 (Talent), 11 (Success) | Strategy, Data Strategy, *All Developer Playbook chapters* |

### By Level

| If You Are... | Your Primary Responsibility in This Guide |
|---------------|------------------------------------------|
| **Executive** | Set direction, define risk appetite, allocate resources, own the narrative |
| **Senior Manager** | Translate strategy into program design, manage vendor relationships, hire and retain |
| **Middle Manager** | Design processes, manage timelines, translate between executives and ICs, protect the team |
| **Individual Contributor** | Ground-truth the ambition, flag technical risks early, build the thing right |

### The Most Important Thing

The single most valuable thing you can do with this chapter is **put the people with the role tags in the same room and work through the questions together**. GeoAI programs fail when:

- Executives set strategy without understanding technical constraints
- Developers build without understanding organizational priorities
- Security reviews happen after development instead of during
- Finance discovers compute costs after commitments are made
- The geospatial domain experts are consulted last instead of first

They succeed when all five perspectives — **CEO, CFO, CSO, CTO, CGO** — and all four levels — **executive, senior manager, middle manager, individual contributor** — hear each other's questions before anyone starts building answers.
